Country Name and Flag

나라 이름과 국기

Quick facts 기본 정보

Official name대한민국 daehanminguk
Republic of Korea
Short name한국 hanguk
In EnglishRepublic of Korea (South Korea)
National flag태극기 taegeukgi
National anthem애국가 aegukga
National flower무궁화 mugunghwa (a pink or light purple flower)

The flag 태극기

The white background means peace and purity. The red and blue circle in the middle means two opposite things that live together (yin and yang).

The 4 groups of black lines in the 4 corners mean sky, earth, water and fire.

The name "Korea"

The word Korea comes from the name of an old kingdom, 고려 goryeo. In English, people say "Korea" or "South Korea".

Koreans often call their own country 한국 or 우리나라 urinara, which means "our country".

Anthem and national flower

The national anthem 애국가 has 4 verses. It is played at ceremonies and before sports games.

The 무궁화 flower blooms for many months, from summer to autumn. Its name means "never ending", and it stands for the patience and strength of Korean people.

Good to know 알아 두면 좋아요

On important national days, like March 1 and August 15, many homes and offices put up the 태극기.

Useful sentences 이렇게 말해요

저는 미국 사람이에요. 한국어를 배워요.
I am American. I am learning Korean.
태극기는 흰색, 빨간색, 파란색, 검은색이 있어요.
The Korean flag has white, red, blue and black.
Learn more더 알아보기

The flag and anthem 국기 예절

When the anthem 애국가 is played at a ceremony, Koreans stand up and put their right hand on their chest. Foreigners can just stand quietly.

Where does "Korea" come from? '코리아'의 유래

The name Korea comes from the kingdom of 고려 (918–1392). Koreans call their country 한국 or 우리나라 (our country).

South Korea and North Korea 남한과 북한

This app talks about 대한민국 (South Korea). North Korea is called 북한. The two sides became separate between 1945 and 1953.

저는 네팔에서 왔어요.
I am from Nepal.

Capital and Population

수도와 인구

Quick facts 기본 정보

Capital서울 seoul (Seoul)
People in Seoulabout 9 million
Total populationabout 51 million
Areaabout 100,000 km² (a little bigger than Portugal)
LanguageKorean 한국어 hangugeo
Writing system한글 hangeul

Seoul

The 한강 river flows through the middle of the city. Seoul has been the capital since 1394.

The city has old palaces, tall buildings and many subway lines. Almost half of the country's people live in Seoul and the cities around it.

People

More than 8 in 10 Koreans live in cities. Now very few babies are born, and the number of old people is growing.

More than 2 million foreigners live in Korea to work or study.

Language and writing

The whole country uses one language, Korean, written in 한글. Many words come from Chinese, and now there are many words from English too.

The name 서울 is a native Korean word meaning "capital". Most other cities have names that come from Chinese characters.

Good to know 알아 두면 좋아요

Korea is a small country, but it has a lot of people: about 51 million, almost as many as England, in a smaller area.

Useful sentences 이렇게 말해요

서울은 한국의 수도예요.
Seoul is the capital of Korea.
서울에는 사람이 정말 많아요.
There are really a lot of people in Seoul.
Learn more더 알아보기

Getting around Seoul 서울 교통

The subway 지하철 has more than 20 lines, with signs in English. Use a 티머니 (T-money) card: buy it at a convenience store and top it up. If you change between bus and subway within 30 minutes, it is free or costs only a little more.

Registering as a foreigner 외국인 등록

Foreigners who stay more than 90 days must register at the immigration office 출입국사무소 within 90 days and get an 외국인등록증 (residence card). You need this card to open a bank account and to get a SIM card.

Must-have apps 필수 앱

Maps: 네이버 지도 or 카카오맵 (Google Maps does not work well in Korea). Chat: 카카오톡. Taxi: 카카오 T.

Say it like this 이럴 때 이렇게 말해요

Asking the way to the station
지하철역이 어디예요?
Where is the subway station?
Topping up your card
티머니 충전해 주세요. 만 원이요.
Please top up my T-money card. 10,000 won.
Asking which subway line
강남역에 가려면 몇 호선을 타요?
Which line do I take to Gangnam Station?

Government and Economy

정부와 경제

Quick facts 기본 정보

SystemDemocratic republic
LeaderPresident 대통령 daetongnyeong: elected by the people for 5 years, only one term
Parliament국회 gukoe
Money원 won (₩)
Bills1,000 · 5,000 · 10,000 · 50,000 won
Coins10 · 50 · 100 · 500 won
Main exportscomputer chips, cars, phones, ships

Economy

After the war ended in 1953, Korea was very poor. Later the economy grew very fast, and Korea became an industrial country.

Companies you probably know, like Samsung, Hyundai, LG and Kia, are Korean companies.

Korea and the world

Korea trades with almost every country in the world, and its products are sold everywhere.

Many international students come to Korea to study and work, and many Korean tourists travel abroad.

Money and prices

The pictures on the bills are important people in history: the 10,000 won bill shows King Sejong, and the 50,000 won bill shows 신사임당 sinsaimdang.

Prices in Korea may be higher than in your country. One meal at a restaurant is about 9,000–12,000 won, and one bus ride is about 1,500 won.

Good to know 알아 두면 좋아요

1,000 won is read 천 원 cheon won, and 10,000 won is read 만 원 man won. Korean counts in units of ten thousand 만. English has no single word for this, so 10,000 is "one 만", not "ten thousand".

Useful sentences 이렇게 말해요

이거 얼마예요?
How much is this?
만 원이에요.
It's 10,000 won.
Learn more더 알아보기

Changing money 환전

It is often best to bring US dollars and change them into 원 in Korea. Money exchange shops 환전소 in the city (for example in Myeongdong) usually give a better rate than the airport. Take your passport with you.

Opening a bank account 은행 계좌

You need your residence card, a Korean phone number and a document from your university or workplace. Banks are open 9:00–16:00, Monday to Friday. A 체크카드 (debit card) works almost everywhere.

Sending money home 해외 송금

To send money to your country, use a bank or an international transfer service 해외송금 in an app. Check the fee and the exchange rate before you send.

Say it like this 이럴 때 이렇게 말해요

At a money exchange
달러를 원으로 바꿔 주세요.
Please change dollars into won.
At the bank
통장을 만들고 싶어요.
I'd like to open an account.
Asking the price
이거 얼마예요?
How much is this?

Land and Sea

땅과 바다

Quick facts 기본 정보

LocationThe southern part of the Korean Peninsula 한반도 hanbando
To the northNorth Korea 북한 bukan
Sea on 3 sidesEast 동해 donghae · West 서해 seohae · South 남해 namhae
Highest mountain한라산 hallasan 1,947 m (on Jeju Island)
Main rivers한강 hangang · 낙동강 nakdonggang (the longest)
Islandsmore than 3,000

Lots of mountains

About 7 in 10 parts of the country are mountains. The mountains in the east are high; the west is lower and has plains.

Koreans love hiking 등산 deungsan on their days off.

The sea

Korea has sea on 3 sides, so Koreans eat a lot of fish and seafood.

There are many big and small islands in the south and the west.

Three different seas

The East Sea 동해 is deep and clear. The West Sea 서해 is shallow, and the tide goes out so far that you can see wide mud flats 갯벌 gaetbeol.

The South Sea 남해 has many islands, and people farm seafood there.

Good to know 알아 두면 좋아요

Most hiking trails in Korea are well made and have signs. But in winter the trails are slippery, so wear hiking boots.

Useful sentences 이렇게 말해요

주말에 산에 가요.
I go to the mountains on the weekend.
우즈베키스탄에는 바다가 없어요.
Uzbekistan has no sea.
Learn more더 알아보기

Sea on three sides 삼면이 바다

The East Sea 동해 is clear and deep, the West Sea 서해 has wide mud flats, and the South Sea 남해 has many small islands. Popular beach cities are Busan and Gangneung.

Hiking 등산

Mountains almost everywhere in Korea have good trails. On weekends, 등산 is very popular. Mountains near Seoul: 북한산, 관악산. You can get there by subway.

Be careful at the sea 바다 안전

You can swim only in July and August, at open beaches. The sea in Korea is colder than you think. Swim only in areas with flags and lifeguards.

Say it like this 이럴 때 이렇게 말해요

Asking about the trail

Enjoying the view

What a beautiful view!

Regions and Cities

지역과 도시

Quick facts 기본 정보

Regions17: cities and provinces
Big cities서울 · 부산 busan · 인천 incheon · 대구 daegu · 대전 daejeon · 광주 gwangju
2nd biggest city부산: a big port in the south
International airport인천공항 incheongonghang (near Seoul)
Government city세종 sejong: many ministries moved here

The capital area

Seoul, Incheon and 경기도 gyeonggido province together are called 수도권 sudogwon. Almost half of the country's people live here.

Many companies, universities and factories are in this area too.

Dialects

Each region has its own dialect 사투리 saturi, just like English sounds different in different parts of Britain or the US.

On TV and in class, people use standard Korean 표준어 pyojuneo, based on Seoul speech.

Travelling between cities

The KTX fast train goes from Seoul to Busan in about 2 and a half hours, and to Jeonju in about 2 hours.

Express buses 고속버스 gosokbeoseu are cheaper and run often. You can buy tickets in an app.

Good to know 알아 두면 좋아요

Korean addresses go from big to small: 도 or 시 → 구 → road → building number. English addresses usually go the other way: number → street → city.

Useful sentences 이렇게 말해요

저는 전주에 살아요.
I live in Jeonju.
서울에서 전주까지 기차로 가요.
I go from Seoul to Jeonju by train.
Learn more더 알아보기

How to read a Korean address 주소 읽기

Addresses go from big to small: province/city → district 구 → road 로/길 → number. To send a package, you need the 5-digit postal code.

Intercity transport 시외 교통

The fast train KTX takes about 2 and a half hours from Seoul to Busan. Express buses 고속버스 are cheaper and go to every city. Book tickets in the 코레일톡 app or at the bus terminal.

International students in Korea 한국의 유학생

International students live all over Korea, not only in Seoul. Most universities, like Jeonju University, have an international office and student clubs where you can make friends.

Say it like this 이럴 때 이렇게 말해요

Buying a train ticket

One ticket to Busan, please.
Giving your address

My address is Jeonju, Jeonbuk.
Asking someone's hometown
고향이 어디예요?
Where is your hometown?

Weather and the Four Seasons

날씨와 사계절

Quick facts 기본 정보

봄 bomMarch–May: warm, flowers bloom
여름 yeoreumJune–August: hot and humid, rainy season 장마 jangma from about late June to July
가을 gaeulSeptember–November: cool and pleasant, leaves turn red and yellow
겨울 gyeoulDecember–February: very cold, Seoul is often below 0°C, some days reach −10°C, snow 눈 nun

For students from warm countries

Some countries have only a rainy season and a dry season, but Korea has 4 seasons.

Korean winters can be much colder than you expect. Get a thick padded jacket 패딩 paeding, a hat and gloves.

Be careful

In spring, some days have a lot of fine dust 미세먼지 misemeonji: wear a mask.

In summer there may be typhoons 태풍 taepung. Check the weather forecast 일기예보 ilgiyebo every day.

What people do each season

In spring, people go to see 벚꽃 beotkkot (cherry blossoms). In summer, they go to the beach and to mountain streams.

In autumn, they go hiking to see the red leaves. In winter, they go skiing and enjoy the snow.

Good to know 알아 두면 좋아요

Inside homes and classrooms it is warm, but outside it is very cold. It is better to wear several layers that are easy to take off and put on.

Useful sentences 이렇게 말해요

오늘 날씨가 정말 추워요.
It's really cold today.
한국은 사계절이 있어요.
Korea has four seasons.
Learn more더 알아보기

Getting ready for winter 겨울 준비

In winter it can be minus 10 degrees. Get a thick padded jacket 패딩, gloves and a scarf. Shops like 다이소 sell cheap winter items.

Fine dust 미세먼지

In spring there is often a lot of fine dust 미세먼지. Check it in a weather app. On 나쁨 (bad) days, wear a KF94 mask.

Rainy season and typhoons 장마와 태풍

Late June to July is 장마. In August–September there may be typhoons 태풍. Your phone will get emergency alert messages 재난문자 in Korean.

It's so cold today.

Will it rain tomorrow?

미세먼지가 심하니까 마스크 쓰세요.
The fine dust is bad, so wear a mask.

Ancient Kingdoms

옛 나라들

Quick facts 기본 정보

고조선 gojoseonThe first kingdom, in history and legend
Three Kingdoms고구려 goguryeo · 백제 baekje · 신라 silla
통일신라 tongilsilla668–935: Silla unites the land
고려 goryeo918–1392: the name Korea comes from this name
조선 joseon1392–1910: the last dynasty, with Seoul as its capital

An old capital

The capital of Silla was 경주 gyeongju. Today it still has many old temples and royal tombs.

In the Goryeo period, Buddhism was very strong.

The Joseon Dynasty

Joseon lasted almost 520 years. Many of the big palaces in Seoul were built in this period.

Most Korean historical dramas tell stories from the Joseon period.

The legend of Dangun

In the legend, 단군 dangun started Gojoseon. His father came down from the sky, and his mother was a bear that became a woman.

October 3, 개천절 gaecheonjeol, is the day to remember this story. Many countries have old stories like this about how they began.

Good to know 알아 두면 좋아요

The Joseon Dynasty (1392) began about 100 years before Columbus sailed to America (1492), and it lasted for more than 500 years.

Useful sentences 이렇게 말해요

경주는 신라의 수도였어요.
Gyeongju was the capital of Silla.
저는 역사 드라마를 좋아해요.
I like historical dramas.
Learn more더 알아보기

The Three Kingdoms 삼국 시대

고구려 (north), 백제 (southwest), 신라 (southeast). Silla united the country in 676.

500 years of Joseon 조선

조선 (1392–1897) built palaces in Seoul, like 경복궁. Most historical dramas 사극 are set in this period.

History trips 역사 여행

Gyeongju = Silla, Buyeo and Gongju = Baekje, Seoul = Joseon. The National Museum of Korea 국립중앙박물관 in Seoul is free.

King Sejong and Hangeul

세종대왕과 한글

Quick facts 기본 정보

Creator세종대왕 sejongdaewang: the 4th king of Joseon
YearCreated in 1443, announced in 1446
Original name훈민정음 hunminjeongeum: "the correct sounds for teaching the people"
Letters24 basic letters: 14 consonants + 10 vowels
Hangeul DayOctober 9, 한글날 hangeullal: a holiday

Why was it made?

Before that, Koreans wrote with Chinese characters 한자 hanja. They were very hard, and ordinary people could not read or write.

So King Sejong made a new, easy writing system for the people.

The shapes of the letters

The consonants show the shape of the mouth and tongue when you make the sound: ㅁ looks like the mouth, ㄴ shows the tongue touching the ridge behind the top teeth.

The vowels come from the sky (a dot), the earth (ㅡ) and a person (ㅣ). The 10,000 won bill has a picture of King Sejong.

Hangeul is easy to learn

Consonants and vowels join together into blocks like little squares: you write from left to right and from top to bottom. Example: ㅎ + ㅏ + ㄴ = 한.

People say a clever person can learn it before lunch, and anyone can learn it in 10 days. Like English, it has consonants and vowels, but it is more regular: each letter almost always has the same sound.

Good to know 알아 두면 좋아요

Want to learn the letters one by one? Go to the 한글 menu in this app.

Useful sentences 이렇게 말해요

한글은 배우기 쉬워요.
Hangeul is easy to learn.
세종대왕이 한글을 만들었어요.
King Sejong created Hangeul.
Learn more더 알아보기

Hangeul really is easy 쉬운 한글

Hangeul has 14 basic consonants and 10 basic vowels. Most people can read it within 1–2 weeks. Try the 한글 section of this app.

Hangeul Day 한글날

October 9 is 한글날, a public holiday. There are events and Hangeul writing contests.

Free Korean classes 무료 한국어 교육

There are free or cheap classes: your university's language center, multicultural family centers, and the 사회통합프로그램 (KIIP) program, which can help with your visa.

Modern Times

근현대

Quick facts 기본 정보

1910–1945Japan ruled Korea
August 15, 1945Korea became free again 광복 gwangbok
1948The south started the Republic of Korea; the north started another country
1950–1953The Korean War 6·25 전쟁 yugio jeonjaeng: it ended with a ceasefire
1960–1990Fast economic growth: "한강의 기적 hangangui gijeok" (the Miracle on the Han River)
1987People began to elect the president directly
1988 · 2002Seoul Olympics · World Cup (together with Japan)

A divided peninsula

South Korea and North Korea are still divided. Between the two countries there is the Demilitarized Zone 비무장지대 bimujangjidae (DMZ).

Many families have lived apart since the war.

Today

In 70 years, Korea changed from a poor country into a developed country.

Korea once received help from other countries. Now it helps other countries in Asia, Africa and around the world.

Korea in the world

Korea has been a member of the United Nations since 1991. In 2018 it held the Winter Olympics in 평창 pyeongchang.

Korea works with many countries: through trade, scholarships for international students and aid programs (KOICA).

Good to know 알아 두면 좋아요

The Korean War is called 6·25 yugio because it started on June 25, 1950. Koreans often name events by their date like this.

Useful sentences 이렇게 말해요

8월 15일은 광복절이에요.
August 15 is Liberation Day.
한국은 빨리 발전했어요.
Korea developed quickly.
Learn more더 알아보기

From poor to developed 한강의 기적

After the war ended in 1953, Korea was very poor. In 50 years it became an industrial country. This is called 한강의 기적 (the Miracle on the Han River).

Your embassy in Korea 주한 대사관

Most countries have an embassy in Seoul. Save your embassy's address and phone number, in case you lose your passport or need help.

Important days 역사 기념일

March 1 삼일절 (protest against Japanese rule in 1919), August 15 광복절 (liberation in 1945), June 25, the day the Korean War started.

Say it like this 이럴 때 이렇게 말해요

Going to your embassy
파키스탄 대사관에 가고 싶어요.
I want to go to the Pakistani embassy.
Asking about a holiday
다음 주 월요일은 쉬는 날이에요?
Is next Monday a holiday?
Talking about history
한국은 빨리 발전했어요.
Korea developed very quickly.

Temples and monks

Most Korean temples 절 jeol are on quiet mountains. Korean Buddhism is Mahayana, unlike the Theravada Buddhism of Myanmar, Thailand or Sri Lanka.

Korean monks 스님 seunim do not walk for morning alms; they eat at the temple and do not eat meat. Buddha's Birthday 부처님오신날 bucheonim osinnal is a holiday, with colorful lanterns.

Churches

Cities have many churches 교회 gyohoe. At night you can see red neon crosses in many places.

People with no religion can still visit a temple or stay at one (temple stay).

Living together

In Korea, many religions live together in peace. Buddha's Birthday and Christmas are both holidays.

In one family, some people may go to a temple, some to a church, and some may have no religion.

Koreans bow instead of hugging or kissing on the cheek. Touching a child's head is not seen as bad in Korea, unlike in some Asian countries.

Don't use elders' names

In Korea, people don't call older people or their boss by name. They use title + 님 instead.

At work, people use family name + title, like 김 부장님 (Kim bujangnim).

Family words for everyone

Koreans call people who are not family "older brother", "older sister" or "aunt". Many cultures in Asia do this too, but in English it sounds unusual.

At restaurants, some people call the woman who cooks 이모 imo (aunt).

Family members

Father 아버지 abeoji (casual 아빠 appa), mother 어머니 eomeoni (casual 엄마 eomma).

Koreans often use 우리 uri (our): 우리 엄마 means "my mom", 우리 회사 means "my company".

You can pay by card or phone almost everywhere.

Shoes off, warm floors

Koreans take off their shoes before going into a home, and some families eat and sleep on the floor.

Korean floors are warm because of the ondol heating system.

Renting a room

To rent a room, you pay a deposit 보증금 bojeunggeum and monthly rent 월세 wolse. You get the deposit back when you move out.

There is also 전세 jeonse: you pay a very large deposit but no monthly rent. This system is rare in other countries.

Music and dance

Like every country, Korea has its own folk songs and dances, and each region has its own style.

Many people around the world learn taekwondo, and it is an Olympic sport.

Traditional games

Children used to play 제기차기 jegichagi (kicking a shuttlecock with the foot), 연날리기 yeonnalligi (flying kites) and 팽이치기 paengichigi (spinning tops).

On holidays, museums and palaces let you play these games.

An island of nature

Jeju has volcanoes, caves, waterfalls and beaches. Many places are World Heritage sites.

Honeymoon couples and tourists love to come here. Jeju's tangerines 귤 gyul are famous.

The Jeju language

Jeju people have a local language that Koreans from other regions find hard to understand.

Strong wind, many stones and many women: people call it the island with "3 many things".

Travelling in Jeju

To travel around Jeju, rent a car or take buses around the island. You need 3–4 days to see it all.

To climb to the top of Hallasan, you must book online in advance, start early in the morning, and it takes almost all day.
